entities.title: Daemon socket handshake
entities.summary: A client opens <state dir>/daemon.sock, sends one JSON line naming its version, roots and stable session, reads one JSON reply line, and then speaks MCP over the same connection.
consumers: zazzle-csharp-indexer serve (Proxy.Connect), from the same or another build of the binary
zazzled (macos/rust/zazzled/), which connects to call the view tool when zazzle reads a .cs file
entities.definition: Hello: {"version": ToolVersion.Text, "roots": ["name=/abs/path" | "/abs/path", ...], "session": stable-caller-session}. Reply: {"ok": true}, or {"ok": false, "error": text} when a root is rejected, or {"ok": false, "restart": bool, "error": text} when the versions differ. Session is optional for older clients; the server creates a random fallback. After ok, newline-delimited JSON-RPC as in src/Mcp/.dev/contracts.json until the client closes.
guarantees: The socket file is readable and writable by its owner only (not set on Windows).
The hello session is used for every usage record produced over the connection, so calls from one agent conversation can be grouped.

A daemon older than the client (ToolVersion.Newer; a -dev build counts as newest) starts draining: it replies restart: true to that client and every later one, and stops once its last client disconnects. A daemon newer than the client replies restart: false with an error telling the user to restart zazzled, and keeps running.
zazzled, told to restart, tries again with backoff from 50 ms up to 1 s for at most 15 s, starting a new daemon when nothing answers.
A second daemon refuses to start while one answers on the socket; a stale socket file with nothing behind it is deleted.
entities.compatibility: The version check is an exact string match on ToolVersion.Text, which every release takes from its tag (macos/dotnet/zazzle-csharp-indexer/.dev/decisions.json, tool-version-source), so a released change to the handshake or to MCP behaviour reaches clients once the old daemon is idle. Builds outside a release all say 0.0.0-dev and are not told apart.
